detail.title: A Bibliometric Analysis of Sustainable Finance Instruments for Small and Medium Size Enterprises
detail.abstract: Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) are playing a key role in offering job creation, market expansion, enhancing innovation, and economic growth. Though the contribution of SMEs is huge in developing nations, they are responsible for emitting 40% of commercial waste, greenhouse gas emissions, and industrial pollution. Sustainable finance instruments are a solution to meet the challenges of socio-economic and environmental issues created by SMEs. Sustainable finance instruments offer funds to accomplish environmentally sustainable projects, to conserve natural resources, combat climate change, protect biodiversity, promote social inclusion, reduce pollution, and promote sustainable development. There are numerous instruments, such as green bonds, green investment funds, sustainability-linked loans, and channel capital towards initiatives, green investment, and ESG-compliant corporate operations available in the market. Among these, sustainable funds are offering financial resources to developing nations. Nowadays, SMEs are encountering numerous challenges like misconceptions about green finance, limited knowledge and expertise in understanding financial resources, and the complexity of securing green finance instruments. All these challenges ruin even when they wish to use green finance to expand operations. SMEs should have an open mindset to embrace the greening process in their operations to make use of the sustainable financial instruments. Previous studies have proved that sustainable finance is being accessed by SMEs in the developing countries, yet the application of sustainable financial instruments on SMEs remains notably underexplored. This underscores the need to fully understand sustainable finance instruments and their application, especially to SMEs in this context. The objective of the study is to adopt bibliometric analysis to assess sustainable financial instruments and SMEs from the Scopus database between 2020 and 2025. This study will highlight the most prolific journals, highly productive authors, and countries that made contributions in the field.

title: Inclusive Leadership Steers Institutional Excellence through Talent Retention and Employee Wellbeing
affiliations: and

detail.title: Inclusive Leadership Steers Institutional Excellence through Talent Retention and Employee Wellbeing
detail.abstract:
Inclusive and responsible leadership has transpired as an essential criterion in moulding a sound institutional culture, precisely in educational scenarios where human resources steer long-term excellence. The rationale of this analysis is rooted in the ever-demanding need for schools to develop leadership practices that value diversity, equality, inclusive decision-making, and ethical stewardship practices that influence talent retention and employee engagement. Inclusive leadership strengthens trust and nurtures loyalty where teachers are not mere employees but the heartbeat of an institution, and their talent chooses to stay, grow and retain.

The purpose of this study is to provide an empirical understanding of how inclusive and responsible leadership moulds talent retention and employee engagement in private schools. Precisely, the study aims to examine the influence of inclusive leadership on teachers’ intention to remain in the institution, to analyse the impact of responsible leadership on employee engagement, to explore the mediating role of job satisfaction and organisational commitment and to provide empirical feedback for strengthening leadership frameworks within the private school system.

A quantitative, descriptive analytical research design will be employed with a structured questionnaire covering the various dimensions of inclusive leadership and talent outcomes. Data will be collected from private school teachers through stratified random sampling. Statistical analysis will provide evidence for the study’s hypotheses.

The originality of this study lies in its holistic and inspiring approach. Presenting leadership not only as a managerial performance but also as a catalyst for emotional connection, institutional excellence, and professional satisfaction, this study contributes a meaningful framework for private schools where teachers feel valued, empowered, and committed to the vision of gaining institutional excellence through inclusive leadership.

title: Pedagogical Innovations in Sustainability Education: A Systematic Literature Review and Bibliometric Analysis
affiliations: and

detail.title: Pedagogical Innovations in Sustainability Education: A Systematic Literature Review and Bibliometric Analysis
detail.abstract: The growing need for graduates who will be able to deal with complex socio-ecological issues, Sustainability Education has become a prominent mandate of higher education systems. While Education for Sustainable Development and Sustainable Development Goals are now embedded within formal curricula globally, dominant transmissive pedagogies continue to support awareness-based learning at the expense of transformative, competency-based learning. This paper provides a systematic synthesis of innovative pedagogical practices in sustainability education, focusing on their alignment with perspectives of sustainability competencies and transformative learning outcomes. A systematic review of the 601 peerreviewed articles indexed in Scopus from 1974 to 2026 was conducted using the PRISMA guidelines and was also supported through bibliometric, thematic and conceptual analyses. The findings indicate that the field is currently in a period of consolidation, as evidenced by a reduction in the growth of publications over time, thematic saturation, and an increasing focus on the application of experiential, problem-based, and transdisciplinary learning pedagogies. However, the data also demonstrate a continuing fragmentation in the field, particularly with respect to the misalignment between pedagogical methods, competency frameworks, assessment practices, and institutional policy integration. There remains a geographical concentration of research in the Global North, with relatively limited empirical validation of long-term learning outcomes and very little integration of digital, socio-cultural, and governance dimensions into sustainability education. The review states that pedagogical innovation is at a turning point, emphasising that further developments in this area require working together across disciplines, using evidence-based approaches, to translate sustainability competencies into large-scale solutions through educational practices and policies; in doing so, higher education institutions will be able to play an important role in facilitating systemic transitions toward sustainability.

title: Imapct of GST Slab Cuts on Affordability and Sustainability of Large-Cap Petrol Cars and Large SUVs

detail.title: Imapct of GST Slab Cuts on Affordability and Sustainability of Large-Cap Petrol Cars and Large SUVs
detail.abstract:
This paper investigates the price structure, buying behavior, and sales performance of large cap cars and SUVs in India following the reduction of the GST slab. While GST reforms were implemented with the aim of boosting growth in the automobile sector, there has been very limited empirical evidence on the impact of such tax changes on high-engine-capacity automobiles above 1500 cc. In such a backdrop, the study will examine the quantum of price reduction that has ensued from the reduction of GST rates, assess the changes in consumer behavior that have resulted due to the said intervention, and study the sales trends for this segment before and after the reform.

In the conceptual framework, the cut in the GST slab is the independent variable, while price reduction, consumer buying behavior, and sales volume are dependent variables. Engine capacity is the moderating variable that determines the strength of these associations. A mixed method approach was used with primary data from structured consumer surveys and secondary data from industry databases, GST policy documents, and official reports on sales. Statistical tools were used to determine whether GST cuts have significantly boosted demand for high capacity petrol vehicles.

The results show that there was a measurable decline in on-road prices following the reduction of the GST rate, which improved the affordability of large SUVs and large-cap petrol cars, thereby increasing interest among consumers. Sales data collected provided evidence of an upwards shift in market demand after this reform, which is especially true for models with over 1500 cc. The hypothesis that a reduction in GST would have positively impacted sales in this category (H1) is therefore proved, providing useful implications for policymakers and automobile manufacturers. Overall, the study contributes to an understanding of how fiscal policy decisions shape consumer behavior, pricing dynamics, and market sustainability in the Indian automobile industry.

title: Exploring the Green HRM as Catalyst for Sustainable Business Model: An Integrated Study of Bibliometric and Systematic Literature Review

Based on 237 records in Scopus, the analysis portrays publication patterns, prominent journals, globally most cited authors, and new research directions to help explain the role played by Green HRM in the sustainability of organizations. The result analysis indicates a significant increase in research momentum, which is caused by the pressure on the global environment and the interest of organizations to incorporate sustainability into HR frameworks, leadership functions, and innovation. The thematic clustering unveils six prevailing sustainable business model directions such as technology-driven, circular economy-oriented, capability-based, governance aligned, behavioural and sector-specific models. These models show the impacts of Green HRM on environmental performance through the creation of green culture, the development of pro-environmental behaviours, the incorporation of digital technologies, and the facilitation of strategic alignment with the sustainability objectives. Another aspect introduced in the study is a synthesis of TCCM, which outlines theoretical, contextual, and methodological trends of the field. Overall, the results are valuable in the context of comprehending the role of HR-related interventions in facilitating business model change providing insights to the researchers and practitioners interested in enhancing environmental sustainability through organization design.

title: Harnessing Artificial Intelligence for Sustainable Finance: Industry Perspectives on the Adoption and Future of Robo-Advisory in India

detail.abstract:
A robo advisory service is an online platform that utilises algorithms and automation to provide investment advice and manage portfolios with minimal or no human intervention. It typically collects basic information about an investor's goals and risk tolerance through a questionnaire and then automatically builds, monitors, and rebalances their investments, usually at a lower cost than human advisors. This study aims to analyse the current state, challenges, and prospects of robo-advisory services, creating sustainable financial systems aligned with SDG 10, which seeks to reduce inequality through expanded access to affordable wealth management.

Questionnaire schedules from semi-structured interviews with fintech leaders reveal that hybrid models, which blend AI analytics with human oversight, are the primary approach. These models offer scalable personalization at a lower cost compared to traditional wealth management, which typically relies on high commissions. Adoption targets urban professionals aged between 30 to 50 in multinationals who are interested in convenience and digital access, yet are hindered by low trust in automation, poor performance records, and a preference for human advisors. Minimal regulatory or technological barriers exist; however, growth demands AI-enhanced personalisation, transparent and straightforward cost communication, and trust building through clear performance tracking dashboards. Fintechs must position robo-advisory services as a more affordable option than traditional advisors, integrate them into their overall investment platforms, and utilize them to offer high-quality wealth management to a broader audience, thereby helping to reduce inequality through increased digital access.

Even though it emerged as a buzz word in academic research, the intellectual structure and evolving knowledge base of impact investing research remain fragmented. This study presents a comprehensive bibliometric analysis to map global research trends, influential contributors, conceptual foundations, and emerging themes in the field. Using data extracted from Scopus database for a time span of 2010-2026, the study examines the conceptual and intellectual structure of the impact investing research using Vosviewer and Biblioshiny. The findings reveal there is a significant growth in scholarly output with a strong conceptual foundation in sustainability. The bibliometric coupling network indicates a mature domain The thematic analysis highlights evolving research fronts such as impact measurement frameworks and behavioural finance. The study offers a structured overview of the field and identifies various themes under the domain. The results also identify critical gaps and propose future research avenues, thereby contributing to strengthening the theoretical and empirical foundations of impact investing.

title: Evaluating the impact of Green Audits on Financial Performance: A Study of PVB Resin Management in the Automobile Industry

detail.title: Evaluating the impact of Green Audits on Financial Performance: A Study of PVB Resin Management in the Automobile Industry
detail.abstract: The rapid growth of the automotive sector has intensified concerns regarding sustainable waste management, particularly for Polyvinyl Butyral (PVB) waste generated from laminated vehicle glass. Despite strong regulatory emphasis on circular economy principles and high end-of-life vehicle recycling targets, PVB waste management remains fragmented due to technological, organizational, and governance challenges. This study examines the influence of Green Audit practices on PVB resin management in the automobile industry using a qualitative, theory-building research design. Data were collected through in-depth semi-structured interviews with industry experts and systematically analyzed using NVivo software following the Gioia methodology, including first-order concepts, second-order themes, and aggregate dimensions. To further explore structural interrelationships among the identified themes, Interpretive Structural Modelling (ISM) was applied to develop a hierarchical framework of key drivers, dependencies, and outcomes associated with Green Audit implementation in PVB waste management. The findings highlight regulatory alignment, managerial commitment, technological preparedness, and stakeholder collaboration as critical enablers influencing effective PVB recycling. The integrated Gioia–ISM approach provides a robust conceptual and cause–effect framework linking Green Audit practices with sustainable PVB management and improved financial performance. The study contributes to environmental governance literature by positioning PVB resin within Green Audit frameworks as a strategic sustainability issue and offers actionable insights for policymakers and industry practitioners to strengthen circular economy initiatives in the automotive sector.

ChatGPT is an artificial intelligence model designed for conversational purposes and it is increasing popularity in digital marketing also. It provides businesses with an essential tool for engaging with customers and optimizing their marketing campaigns. Examining ChatGPT's effect on the customer engagement in the context of digital marketing is the primary goal of this study. This paper synthesizes existing literature to analyze the impact of ChatGPT on customer engagement in the digital marketing domain. title: On the Roles of GenAI in Theory Building and on Mileva Marić, Einstein's Wife
affiliations: Warsaw School of Economics (SGH)

detail.title: On the Roles of GenAI in Theory Building and on Mileva Marić, Einstein's Wife
detail.abstract: This paper explores the roles that generative artificial intelligence (genAI) can fulfil in the theory-building process within the social sciences, drawing an analogy with Mileva Marić's contributions to Albert Einstein's scientific work. Whilst existing literature acknowledges genAI as a cognitive partner in knowledge generation, it lacks systematic frameworks for understanding its diverse functions in theory construction. Based on autoethnographic research in management sciences, this study identifies four distinct roles: the proficient encyclopaedist (synthesising dispersed knowledge across disciplines), the crazy innovator (generating creative ideas at scale), the meticulous reviewer (providing critical feedback), and the drunken cartographer (attempting to structure theoretical relationships). The findings emphasise that genAI operates most effectively through iterative, human-in-the-loop processes, where the researcher's judgment remains central to evaluating, interpreting, and curating generated content. The paper contributes to the literature by providing a conceptual framework that shifts the debate from tool-level discussions to epistemic considerations of how genAI participates in theory construction in the social sciences.

title: Understanding Sustainable Fashion Consumption Among Generation Z: An ADO Framework Analysis of the Value-Action Gap
affiliations: , ,  and

detail.title: Understanding Sustainable Fashion Consumption Among Generation Z: An ADO Framework Analysis of the Value-Action Gap
detail.abstract:
Sustainable fashion is pivotal for decarbonizing apparel systems, and Generation Z is recognized as environmentally conscious. Yet, a persistent value–action gap shapes their consumption, with intentions failing to yield purchases. Prior research examines attitudes, values, and social drivers, but evidence remains fragmented, lacking synthesis mapping antecedents to decisions/outcomes for Gen-Z.

This study addresses this gap by consolidating high-quality empirical research to identify the mechanisms that reinforce or inhibit sustainable fashion decisions among Gen Z, offering theoretical and managerial insights grounded in the ADO (Antecedents–Decisions–Outcomes) framework.

Following PRISMA-2020 guidelines, a Scopus search of ABDC A/A* journals (2010–2025) screened 1028 records and yielded 32 peer-reviewed studies. A qualitative ADO synthesis was conducted, supported by VOSviewer and Biblioshiny bibliometric analysis to map intellectual structures, thematic clusters, and emerging research fronts.

Findings show that personal antecedents-environmental knowledge, ethical identity, and self-expressive values combine with socio-cultural influences such as peer norms and influencer communication to strengthen sustainability intentions. However, the decision stage is constrained by affordability, convenience, trust deficits, and greenwashing scepticism, often pushing Gen Z toward accessible fast-fashion alternatives. Outcomes reveal suppressed sustainable behaviours despite high stated concern, with bibliometric networks identifying “sustainable consumption” as a motor theme and signalling a declining emphasis on CSR-driven messaging.
The study extends sustainable consumption literature by developing the Socio-Cultural-Personal (SCP) schema, which clarifies where intention–action disconnects emerge within the consumer journey. The review demonstrates that decision-level frictions and not attitude deficits primarily drive the gap, underscoring the need for transparent branding, credible sustainability claims, and affordability-oriented green marketing strategies.

For practitioners, the findings highlight social media’s dual role in enabling and undermining sustainable choices. For scholars, the results offer a foundation for expanding the TCM (Theories–Contexts–Methods) agenda, particularly across cross-cultural and digital consumption contexts.

title: The Moderating Role Frustration Effect Sunk Costs On Repurchase Intention

detail.title: The Moderating Role Frustration Effect Sunk Costs On Repurchase Intention
detail.abstract: Cross-border retail presents challenges that generate recurrent frustrations. Paradoxically, consumers continue purchasing on these platforms. This study investigates how frustration moderates the effect of sunk costs on repurchase intention, analyzing 447 Brazilian consumers via PLS-SEM and Multigroup Analysis. The results reveal that frustration intensifies psychological lock-in to prior financial investments, acting as a cognitive dissonance reduction mechanism, especially for light users. Heavy users, however, rely on service quality and exhibit emotional immunity. The findings raise ethical implications for retail: retention based on cognitive biases and loss aversion creates an exploitative "spurious loyalty." Managers and policymakers must mitigate monetary barriers and focus on customer service excellence, replacing lock-in tactics with authentic satisfaction

title: Fiduciary Governance Without Beneficiaries
affiliations: Pace University - School of Law

detail.title: Fiduciary Governance Without Beneficiaries
detail.abstract:
Trusts increasingly operate at the boundary between private ordering and public law. In the wake of Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization and the spread of state fetal-personhood regimes, settlors and fiduciaries now confront the possibility that embryos or other unborn entities may be treated as legally cognizable beneficiaries. At the same time, trust law has moved toward increasingly privatized governance, most prominently through silent trusts and proxy-based administration that limit beneficiary knowledge and judicial oversight. Together, these developments press trust law to confront a form of beneficiary uncertainty that concerns not only when an interest will attach, but whether it will ever attach to a determinate person at all. This Article examines the interaction of these developments through the lens of recent changes to trust law in Delaware, a leading jurisdiction that other states are likely to follow. 

The Article makes three claims. First, existing trust law already accommodates embryonic beneficiaries without doctrinal innovation, given longstanding tools for administering future and contingent interests. Second, the existence of embryonic beneficiaries raises the question of whether (and how) a beneficial interest can exist where attachment to an identifiable beneficiary may never emerge. This unknowability, combined with silent trust regimes, produces a form of fiduciary governance characterized by ontological indeterminacy rather than mere temporal delay. Third, the normalization of proxy-mediated enforcement under these conditions reconfigures institutional justification of fiduciary obligation by severing fiduciary power from beneficiary-centered accountability. 

By shifting attention away from debates over fetal status and toward the design of fiduciary governance, the Article shows how silent-trust architecture functions as a private-law response to expanding biological contingency. It concludes that the convergence of fetal-personhood regimes with silent trusts exposes a broader legitimacy problem for fiduciary law in an era of privatized governance and sustained non-knowledge.

title: Ban Cookie Banners: A Case Study in Tech Regulation
affiliations: St. John's University - School of Law

detail.title: Ban Cookie Banners: A Case Study in Tech Regulation
detail.abstract:
Few experiences on the modern internet are as universally reviled as the cookie banner. They clutter websites with pop-ups, interrupt user flow, make information harder to access, and demand repetitive, meaningless clicks. What was once heralded as a tool to advance individual autonomy and privacy has, in practice, become a daily annoyance that breeds cynicism with the very concept of consent itself. Cookie banners do not empower; they weary. They do not inform; they obscure. They do not prevent surveillance; they normalize it. 

The tragedy of the cookie banner is that it embodies the best intentions but worst solutionism of modern regulation: the fantasy that complex problems such as digital surveillance can be solved by forcing individuals to click "I agree." At best, this fantasy has produced a regime of performative compliance that neither informs users nor limits data exploitation and degrades internet usability. But at worst, it has crowded out more substantive reforms by offering the illusion of protection while leaving surveillance capitalism intact. Government can point to the highly visible cookie banner and declare its promise met in addressing data privacy issues. Industry, now that a compliance solution has been agreed on and normalized, prefers a known system with which they can easily comply and are unmotivated to push for a reform. While users, faced with endless click-throughs, learn not to assert their rights but to surrender them reflexively. In this sense, cookie banners are not merely bad design. They are a cautionary tale of regulatory failure. Born from European data protection laws, exported worldwide through market forces, and mirrored in other government regulations, banners represent the triumph of ritual over reality in technology law.

To this end, this Article argues one thing and one thing only: that cookie banners should be abolished. They do not protect privacy, they erode meaningful consent, and they impose unnecessary costs on information access, usability, and even the environment. Most of all, their existence stands in the way of future progress and a new regulatory solution. In order to understand how regulation can go so wrong—and how to move beyond it—this article traces the history of cookie banner mandates, catalogues their failures, and makes a simple plea: to end cookie banners so the law can move towards new interventions to protect individuals' privacy with something more than a hollow click.

title: The Oneness of Information: Informational Gravity and a Call for Horizontal Integration in Information Science

detail.title: The Oneness of Information: Informational Gravity and a Call for Horizontal Integration in Information Science

declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. Conducted as part of PhD studies at the University of North Texas.

detail.abstract: Russell Ackoff's Data-Information-Knowledge-Wisdom (DIKW) hierarchy remains foundational to Information Science. Its linear progression was adequate at the time. As we transition from the information era into the knowledge era, it is critical to revise and address potential enhancements to the framework and to understand how contemporary knowledge flows. As Artificial Intelligence excels in vertical specialization and technical data processing, the discipline of Information Science faces a critical pivot. This paper proposes The Oneness of Information, a theoretical extension positing that a critical phenomenon occurs precisely when data transforms into information through human meaning-making. Because the capacity to create and interpret meaning is universally shared among humans, and because all meaning refers to an ontologically interconnected reality, this moment of transformation inherently connects all humanity. We establish what we name Informational Gravity: a convergent tendency driven by the epistemological imperative to reduce uncertainty, in which ideas naturally attract and integrate across disciplinary, industrial, and cultural boundaries. Grounded in Shannon's information theory at the individual level and Bertalanffy's General Systems Theory at the systemic level, this gravity exists in two states: Concealed Gravity (connections invisible due to barriers in time or technology) and Identified Gravity (connections realized and acted upon). We further introduce the Methodology of Horizontal Integration, a practical framework organized across three organizational pillars: (1) Project Management strategies, where it promotes scope expansion across the analysis phase common to virtually all project and management frameworks, which-despite originating in different domains-share common structural patterns yet remain vertically constrained; (2) Analysis of information flow in Organizational Culture, where it redefines Change Management as a social-gravitational process; and (3) Information Systems, where it prioritizes semantic continuity over mere technical connectivity. This framework identifies a paradigm shift from vertical learning (deep specialization within silos) to horizontal learning (cross-disciplinary knowledge sharing enabled by large language models and democratized data access). Consequently, Information Science emerges as a meta-discipline uniquely positioned to navigate, validate, standardize, and facilitate knowledge flows across all fields, training a new generation of professionals who adopt the Information Integrator paradigm-a horizontal lens applicable across all professional roles and organizational levels. Implications for educational design, organizational knowledge management, curriculum development, and future interdisciplinary research are discussed, along with three formal research propositions for empirical validation.

detail.abstract: Performance measurement systems are commonly treated as instruments of transparency and control. Yet embedded longitudinal observation in hierarchical organizations suggests a paradox: as dashboards approach representational perfection—compliance rates rising, reporting gaps disappearing, indicators turning uniformly green—organizational knowing may decline. This paper theorizes this paradox as metric blindness: a structural epistemic condition in which increasing measurement sophistication reduces epistemic accuracy by privileging codified legibility over lived operational intelligence. Drawing on a twenty-year longitudinal insider study in a large private security organization operating in a high-risk North African context, the analysis develops a mechanism-based explanation of how metric blindness stabilizes over time. Three mechanisms are traced: (1) shadow systems that preserve non-legible intelligence outside formal visibility; (2) escalation filtering, in which anomalies become non-formulable or travel upward only through forced translation that neutralizes their risk content; and (3) confidence–anxiety divergence, where leadership infers governability from dashboard calmness while frontline coordination absorbs hidden strain. The paper extends work on metric reactivity and audit cultures by shifting from behavioral "gaming" to architectural epistemic asymmetry; it advances silence theory by distinguishing intentional silence from structural silence; and it positions metric blindness as organized ignorance produced by design rather than intent. Finally, it introduces dual visibility structures as a theoretical governance principle for epistemic resilience: sustaining the paradox of accountability and learning by separating evaluative and exploratory epistemic channels.

detail.abstract: This paper reviews seven contemporary official guidelines to cost-benefit analysis (CBA) with respect to eight major cost-benefit issues drawing on the latest edition of the major CBA textbook for guidance, although not complete authority. The guidelines are those by UK Treasury, European Commission, U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, New Zealand Treasury, Infrastructure Australia, NSW State Treasury, and Victorian State Department of Treasury and Finance. The eight major issues discussed are the issue of standing, core valuation principles, the scope of CBA with reference to potential additional economic benefits, changes in real values over time, the marginal excess tax burden, the social discount rate, use of benefit-cost ratios, and treatment of risk. While all the guidelines are quality guides to CBA, the paper finds that there is room for improved discussion and practice at various points in each of these guidelines.

detail.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies. The use of AI-based systems in the context of online retailing is becoming more and more common in order to improve the interaction between consumers and streamline the decision-making process. However, with this increased uptake, there is still a gap in the literature considering the effects that AI has on the online lives of consumers and their decision to purchase in a explicitly consumer-focused way. Using the Social Response Theory as a conceptual framework, the current research proposes research questions that examine how the antecedents associated with technology influence the formation of AI-mediated consumer experiences and their further effects on buying intentions. A positivist quantitative approach will be used to gather data on 500 online consumers who have already used AI-based technologies. The hypotheses are tested using Structural Equation Modelling (SEM) as the cross-sectional empirical study complemented by descriptive statistics and Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA). The predicted results will build on the existing theories of consumer experience by explaining the effect of AI-based interactions on consumer decision-making processes based on mediating and moderating processes. The research is valuable to the academic community as it provides a more in-depth insight into AI-mediated experiences of consumers in the context of online stores. It also presents viable implications to marketers and companies that are trying to develop and execute more consumer-focused, result-based AI in online trading settings.

detail.abstract: In this paper, we describe the architecture and deployment of a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) environment that leverages NVIDIA's Inference Microservices (NIM) suite-including the NIM Cache for pre-caching model profiles and NIM Service for serving inference workloads tightly coupled with a GPU-accelerated Milvus vector database. Our platform is deployed on a three-node Kubernetes cluster comprised of Dell PowerEdge R760xa servers, each provisioned with a single NVIDIA L40 GPU. Despite this modest hardware footprint, we achieve high-throughput semantic search and generative inference at scale. Central to our approach is GPU time-slicing, which partitions GPU compute cycles among multiple workloads to support dynamic sharing, paired with Kubernetes-native device scheduling to instantiate virtual GPU replicas across summarization, embedding, and ranking microservices. This strategy enables near-real-time semantic retrieval and generation, fully saturating GPU capabilities without necessitating additional physical GPUs.

title: Adaptive Tokenomics: A Systems Engineering Approach to Programmable Incentive Design

declarations.declarationOfInterest: N/A

detail.abstract:
Token design lacks a coherent discipline. Projects assemble mechanisms from precedent, failures are attributed to market conditions rather than predictable design flaws, and no established field integrates the economics, control theory, game theory, and constitutional design that token systems require. We frame the resulting practice as systems engineering: coordinating autonomous agents under uncertainty while distributing ownership to contributors without centralized enforcement. What distinguishes protocols from historical private currency issuance is programmable enforcement of issuance rules and reconfiguration of the capital-labor boundary that results when verified contribution generates ownership. 

We develop MeshNet, a fictional but empirically parameterized decentralized wireless protocol that specifies five integrated mechanisms: productive staking, reputation-weighted governance, burn-mint value capture, conviction voting, and PID (proportional-integral-derivative)-controlled adaptive emissions. Parameters are calibrated to Helium hardware economics, Filecoin collateral ratios, and governance data from 12 DePIN and DeFi protocols. A 240-run agent-based ensemble, supplemented by 566 sensitivity and adversarial runs, stress-tests these mechanisms over five years under four macroeconomic scenarios. 

The simulation yields three principal findings. First, adaptive emission functions as insurance: the PID controller compresses worst-case variance by 6× (coefficient of variation from 0.544 to 0.087 under competitor shock) while sustaining 8,880 nodes at the 5th percentile versus 1,049 under static policy. Second, this advantage is conditional: bull markets produce identical outcomes, and the engineering premium emerges only under sustained contraction. Third, without pre-planned guardrails the controller can trigger integral wind-up, reinforcing the case for simulation-first design methodology. The methodology generalizes to any token economy that must coordinate autonomous agents under uncertainty.

detail.abstract: Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) are vital to economic growth and sustainability, yet most existing Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) scoring systems focus on large, publicly listed firms, leaving SMEs largely overlooked. This research introduces a new ESG scoring methodology specifically designed for SMEs, which addresses the challenges of limited disclosure, sector-specific materiality, and data quantifiability. Using publicly available information and expert input, we construct a questionnaire-based ESG index aligned with the Sustainability Accounting Standards Board (SASB) framework to ensure sector-specific materiality. The methodology applies advanced optimization techniques to determine indicator weights and uses multiple mapping functions to generate robust, interpretable ESG scores. The findings contribute to advancing methodologies for ESG scoring in SMEs and inform policy discussions on enhancing sustainability disclosures tailored to SMEs' operational contexts.

detail.abstract: The Andaman and Nicobar Islands in India, with their unique geographical isolation and limited infrastructure, present a distinct environment for Small and Medium-sized Enterprises. In such a context, digitalization has the potential to transform how local businesses operate, connect with markets, and manage resources. This study aims to explore the determinants that influence the impact of digitalization on SMEs operating in this ecologically sensitive and logistically challenged region. A structured questionnaire was developed with five core dimensions such as awareness, training, usage, investment, and the impact. Primary data was collected from 53 registered SMEs during May 2025. This study used Descriptive Statistics, ANOVA and Correlation to get insights about the data. Further, using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM), this study validated the relationships among constructs and assessed the influence of awareness, training, usage and investment on the impact. The SEM results reveal statistically significant relationships, indicating that awareness and training positively influence digital usage, training drives usage, digital usage significantly boosts investment and investment strongly impacts overall digital outcomes for SMEs. The study underscores the need for structured training programs, policy support, and accessible digital infrastructure to enhance the digital maturity of island-based SMEs.

תקציר בעברית: דמוקרטיות ליברליות מתמודדות עם אתגר מבני במדיניות הגירה ואינטגרציה: נאמנות חוקתית - המחויבות היסודית לנורמות משפטיות, לגיטימיות המדינה ושלטון החוק - אינה ניתנת להעברה באמצעות קורסי אוריינטציה בלבד. מאמר זה טוען שנאמנות כזו מוטמעת במערכות מוסדיות שהתפתחו במהלך מאות שנים של אבולוציה תלוית-מסלול, הנושאות משקל נורמטיבי הנגזר הן מניסיון היסטורי עמוק והן מטראומה קולקטיבית ספציפית.

עולים חדשים ואוכלוסיות פנימיות לא-משולבות עשויים ללמוד את הכללים מבלי לגשת להקשר שהופך את הכללים למחייבים נורמטיבית. יתרה מזאת, האתגר חורג מעבר לפרטים ומגיע ל”חיקוי מוסדי,” שבו קולקטיבים לא-ליברליים מאמצים את הצורות החיצוניות של החברה האזרחית כדי להסוות סדרים נורמטיביים מקבילים.

מדיניות אינטגרציה נוכחית נעה בין שתי טעויות: אוניברסליזם עיוור-הקשר מניח שמחויבויות ליברליות נגישות באופן מובן מאליו ללא תיווך, ומייצר ציפיות אופטימיות מדי וחוסר השקעה מוסדית; רטוריקה הדרתית מתייחסת לאתגרי האינטגרציה כעדות ליכולת מולדת בלתי-מספיקה, וסוגרת את האפשרות לשילוב אמיתי.

לבחינה אמפירית של דינמיקות אלה, המאמר מתמקד במקרה המזרחי כמקרה בוחן מרכזי: בין 1948 ל-1956, כ-700,000 יהודים ממדינות ערב וצפון אפריקה הגיעו לישראל הצעירה. הם נתקלו במערכת מוסדית שיצרה ״הדרה לא מכוונת״ ודרשה מהם מחיקה תרבותית תוך מניעת השתתפות אמיתית בכוח המוסדי.
מסגרת ניתוח ייחודית: כדי להבין את כישלון האינטגרציה המזרחי, המאמר מציע ארבע עדשות ניתוח מבניות שפועלות במקביל: (1) חוסר התאמה בהון חברתי (Social Capital Mismatch) - המוסדות נבנו עבור “הון חברתי מגשר” בעוד שליהודי המזרח היה “הון חברתי קושר” עשיר שנתפס כשבטי; (2) ביטחוניזציה של תרבות (Securitization of Culture) - הערביות של המזרחים שיקפה את זהות האויב הקיומי, ויצרה “מחיקה הגנתית”; (3) גירעון באוריינות מוסדית (Institutional Literacy Deficit) - יהודי המזרח הגיעו ללא הידע השבשתיקה של איך דמוקרטיה פועלת; (4) מורשת אוריינטליסטית (Orientalist Inheritance) - האשכנזים הפנימו את הדעות הקדומות האירופאיות על העולם הערבי.

למרות זאת, המאמר מדגיש: זה לא היה קולוניאליזם במובן הקלאסי. האשכנזים לא פעלו מתוך כוונה זדונית לדכא או לנצל. הם פעלו מתוך אידיאולוגיה אמיתית של בניית אומה דמוקרטית, ויתרו על שפותיהם שלהם (יידיש) למען העברית הלאומית, ומנהיגים כמו בן-גוריון עברו לפריפריה למרות חוסר הנוחות האישית. הבעיה הייתה Dismissal מבני, לא זדון.

השלכות: כישלונות האינטגרציה לא הניבו משבר מיידי. הם יצרו אוכלוסיות שהיחסים שלהן למדינה היו מעוותים - מועברים לילדים ונכדים, ומתפרצים כמשבר חוקתי 70 שנה מאוחר יותר. המקרה המזרחי התפרץ כמשבר לגיטימציה סביב כוח שיפוטי במשבר הרפורמה השיפוטית של 2023.

הלקח המרכזי: אינטגרציה אינה ניתנת לקיצור דרך הכללה הצהרתית. קיבולת קליטה היא סופית ויש לכבד אותה. החלופה לאינטגרציה אמיתית, תובענית, מדודה-דורית אינה יציבות אלא קרע חוקתי דחוי. ההחלטות על אינטגרציה שמתקבלות היום יניבו את תוצאותיהן לא ב-2030 אלא ב-2090.

English Abstract:  Liberal democracies face a structural challenge in migration and integration policy: constitutional loyalty—the foundational commitment to legal norms, state legitimacy, and the rule of law—cannot be transmitted through orientation courses alone. This article argues that such loyalty is embedded in institutional systems that developed over centuries of path-dependent evolution, carrying normative weight derived from deep historical experience and specific collective trauma. New immigrants and unintegrated internal populations may learn the rules without accessing the context that makes those rules normatively binding. Furthermore, the challenge extends beyond individuals to "institutional mimicry," whereby illiberal collectives adopt the external forms of civil society to mask parallel normative orders. Current integration policy oscillates between two errors: context-blind universalism assumes that liberal commitments are self-evidently accessible without mediation, producing overly optimistic expectations and insufficient institutional investment; exclusionary rhetoric treats integration challenges as evidence of inherent incapacity, foreclosing the possibility of genuine inclusion. For empirical examination, this article focuses on the Mizrahi case as a central test case: between 1948 and 1956, approximately 700,000 Jews from Arab and North African countries arrived in young Israel, encountering an institutional system that created "unintentional exclusion"—demanding cultural erasure while preventing genuine participation in institutional power. The article proposes four analytical lenses: (1) Social capital mismatch: Institutions were designed for "bridging capital" (weak ties, generalized trust), while Mizrahi Jews possessed rich "bonding capital" (familial networks, particularized trust) that was pathologized as "tribal"; (2) Securitization of culture: The Arabic language and cultural attributes of Mizrahi Jews mirrored the existential enemy, creating "defensive erasure"—forced de-Arabization driven not by racism but by genuine fear; (3) Institutional literacy deficit: Mizrahi Jews arrived without the tacit knowledge of how democracy functions, having been excluded from political participation under the Ottoman millet system and authoritarian monarchies for generations; (4) Orientalist legacy: Ashkenazi elites internalized European prejudices about the Arab world despite themselves being victims of those same European prejudices against Jews. Despite this, the article emphasizes: this was not colonialism in the classical sense. Ashkenazim did not act from malicious intent to oppress or exploit. They acted from genuine ideology of nation-building, sacrificed their own languages (Yiddish) for national Hebrew, and leaders like Ben-Gurion moved to the periphery despite personal discomfort. The problem was structural dismissal—not malice. Implications: Integration failures did not produce immediate crisis. They created populations whose relationship to the state was distorted—transmitted to children and grandchildren, erupting as constitutional crisis 70 years later. The Mizrahi case erupted as a legitimacy crisis around judicial power in the 2023 judicial reform crisis. The central lesson: Integration cannot be shortcut through declarative inclusion. Absorption capacity is finite and must be respected. The alternative to genuine, demanding, generationally-measured integration is not stability but deferred constitutional rupture. Decisions made today on integration will yield results not in 2030 but in 2090.

title: Financial Fragility Indexes for Latin American Countries using the Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition Filtering Method
affiliations: Banco de la Republica, Tilburg University and Tilburg University

detail.title: Financial Fragility Indexes for Latin American Countries using the Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition Filtering Method
detail.abstract: This paper studies the financial fragility of seven Latin American countries, in a period in which two global episodes hit financial markets and economies worldwide: the great financial crisis (2007-2009) and the COVID-19 shock (2020-2021). Given the relatively short time spans of financial data available for developing economies, the traditional smoothing methods, which require use of long-time series to obtain reliable results, are not expected to deliver satisfactory results. Instead, we propose a new methodological approach for this type of analysis, i.e., the Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition (EEMD) filtering method. We demonstrate its superior performance on individual financial indicators and then aggregate these indicators at the country level and by type of indicator. Our results show that the financial fragility of these countries was increasing before and during the first episode, while for the other episode it started to increase during the lockdown period but suddenly fell in response to the measures taken by the economic authorities. The policy implications of this study point to the need for a proper assessment of financial fragility levels, as this will allow central banks to be better equipped to implement macroprudential measures to mitigate the effects of financial instability in crisis periods as well as to achieve a rapid recovery from its negative effects.

title: Federal Surveys Undercount People with Disabilities as Defined by the Amendments to the Americans with Disabilities Act
affiliations: U.S. Office of Research, Social Security Administration

detail.title: Federal Surveys Undercount People with Disabilities as Defined by the Amendments to the Americans with Disabilities Act
detail.abstract: Disability measurement in federal surveys aligns with the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990 (ADA) by focusing on major life activity limitations but has not evolved to align with the ADA Amendments Act of 2008, which expands the definition of major life activities to include major bodily functions. I find that people who ever had a major bodily function limitation were at least 30 percentage points less likely to be identified as having a disability, compared with people with major life activity limitations as defined before the amendments. The finding shows a disparity in disability identification in federal surveys. This disparity can be eliminated by expanding the scope of disability measurement to include major bodily function limitations. I quantify this expansion would increase the disability prevalence estimate among people aged 18–64 in the 2023 American Community Survey from 11 percent to roughly 27 percent, equivalent to 33 million additional people identified as having a disability.

title: Liquidity, Volatility, and Price Discovery in Indian Mid-Cap Stocks: Evidence from NSE using Daily and Intraday Indicators
affiliations: and

detail.title: Liquidity, Volatility, and Price Discovery in Indian Mid-Cap Stocks: Evidence from NSE using Daily and Intraday Indicators
detail.abstract:
The functioning of financial markets is profoundly influenced by the relationship between liquidity, volatility, and price discovery efficiency. Understanding how these factors interact is crucial for assessing the overall quality and informational efficiency of equity markets. This study investigates these dynamics within India’s mid-cap equity segment, emphasizing how liquidity and trading activity affect volatility and the efficiency of price adjustment processes. Using daily data for a sample of NSE Mid-Cap and Large-Cap stocks over a six-month period from January 2025 to June 2025, the study employs descriptive, correlation and regression analyses to evaluate differences in market quality. Liquidity is measured using trading volume and turnover ratio, while volatility is derived from daily stock returns. Price discovery efficiency is assessed through the correlation between individual stock returns and their respective index movements.

The research aims to reveal how variations in liquidity and trading activity influence volatility patterns and the speed at which information is incorporated into prices. It is expected that mid-cap stocks will demonstrate relatively higher volatility and lower liquidity than large-cap counter parts, reflecting greater sensitivity to information shocks and trading imbalances. Furthermore, higher trading activity is anticipated to enhance price stability and improve the overall efficiency of price discovery.

This study contributes to the growing body of literature on market microstructure in emerging economies by focusing on an underexplored segment of the Indian equity market. Its insights will be valuable to investors, regulators, and policymakers seeking to strengthen liquidity mechanisms and promote efficient and transparent market structures. These findings also hold significance for the cost and management accounting community, as efficient liquidity conditions and stable price discovery directly support more accurate valuation, better capital allocation, and informed managerial financial decisions.

title: Estimating the Likely Harms from Global Warming: A Fresh Look at Accounting for Adaptation and Resilience, and Recommendations for a Bottom-Up Approach

detail.title: Estimating the Likely Harms from Global Warming: A Fresh Look at Accounting for Adaptation and Resilience, and Recommendations for a Bottom-Up Approach

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No relationship to other organizations.
declarations.funderStatement: No outside funding.

detail.abstract:
We urgently need to determine a reasonable ballpark estimate for the likely harms from global warming before we commit to a set of mitigation policies, because aggressive mitigation of global warming by forcing a quick transition to low-emissions technologies could be very costly and disruptive to human society, while slow action could leave us vulnerable to serious harms from climate change.  I attempt here to improve our understanding of the likely harms if we do nothing to reduce global warming.  This paper does three things: (1) evaluates the literature on the harms from global warming, and finds it lacking; (2) introduces an alternative framework for analyzing the harms, that incorporates adaptation and resilience, and is based on a bottom-up approach with multiple metrics and types of harms; and (3) provides a very preliminary assessment of the likely harms under a business-as-usual scenario.  I provide some new perspectives on the debate, namely that human society has developed a tremendous resilience and ability to adapt to known weather events, and yet global warming will generate new kinds of weather events that could cause significant harm because of their surprise factor.  This paper is primarily about the methodology of estimating harms – it does not provide firm conclusions or numerical estimates of the likely harms, especially in the long run where there is great uncertainty about possible climate changes and harms. It also points out certain issues that need to be addressed, and key questions to be answered, for those who assert that the harms will be high, or that the harms will be low.  

In the literature, there is major disagreement on the size of likely harms from global warming, with scientists and activists warning that global warming is an existential threat requiring an immediate transition to non-carbon emissions technologies, while economists and modelers’ Integrated Assessment Models (IAMs) predicting much smaller harms, about 0-4% of GDP income reduction for a global temperature increase of 2-4°C.  I argue that neither side provides a reasonable forward-looking methodology for measuring the likely harms to human society from climate change.  In particular we should account for how human resilience and adaptation can significantly reduce the impact of most foreseeable climate events and changes, but we should be aware that surprise and extreme events and major climate changes could cause large harms. 

I recommend that an alternative methodology be used, that builds a bottom-up approach with a more granular analysis based on likely mechanisms of harm.  The analysis should be performed for each type of climate event of concern, such as storms, heat and cold waves, floods, droughts, wildfires, and sea level rise.  Rather than relying on a single metric of harm, I recommend using multiple metrics for measuring harms, including deaths, damages, subpopulation harms, disruption, discomfort, and biodiversity, with the emphasis on deaths and the impact on human social welfare.  Key factors that affect the likely size of harms include the resilience of human society to various likely climate events; the likelihood of adaptation to observed changes; the ability of climate change to surprise us with new and unexpected events; and the presence of certain human co-factors: poverty and the level of development, the impact of war, and government mismanagement. 

The paper provides some tentative conclusions that global warming will increasingly generate significant harms to our way of life, but is unlikely to cause huge casualties in the short run, especially in the developed world.  Our improved ability to adapt and handle most adverse climate events is evidenced by the decline of peacetime famines in the last 200 years.  Unless a new catastrophic scenario becomes apparent, this is not an existential threat, but we may end up miserable with a significant loss of life, income and quality of life.  However, since we are entering uncharted territory, there is a significant level of uncertainty concerning the likely harms we face in the long run.

title: Reconciling Risk and Workers’ Rights: The EU’s Risk-Based Approach to Algorithmic Management and Its Implications for Labour Law
affiliations: Universita degli Studi di Torino

detail.title: Reconciling Risk and Workers’ Rights: The EU’s Risk-Based Approach to Algorithmic Management and Its Implications for Labour Law

contentType.other: Final unformatted version of a paper forthcoming in the European Labour Law Journal (after peer review)

detail.abstract: This paper examines the expansion of the EU's risk-based approach to the governance of algorithmic management and its implications for labour law. Risk-based regulation - as embodied in the GDPR, the AI Act, and the Platform Work Directive - relies on anticipatory and context-sensitive mechanisms, most notably impact assessments, to identify and manage risks before harm occurs. These techniques remain largely unfamiliar to labour law, which has traditionally relied on a rightsbased approach based on prescriptive norms generally aimed at the outright prevention of harm. As a result, scholars have expressed concern that importing a logic of risk tolerance into the domain of workers' rights may erode established protections and trigger deregulatory drift. After analysing the core features of the EU's risk-based approach and its interaction with labour law, the paper argues that these tensions can be generally reconciled through interpretation. When impact assessments concern workers' rights, they should be read as requiring risk elimination rather than mere mitigation, thereby aligning risk-based regulation with the protective core of labour law. Although enforcement challenges remain and are primarily a matter for policy intervention, the paper contends that risk-based regulation - if properly framed and interpreted - does not necessarily undermine labour law's foundational logic, but can enhance its anticipatory and preventive capacity in the governance of algorithmic management.

title: Fiscal News and the Macroeconomy: Evidence from UK Budget Announcements
affiliations: European University Institute and University of Glasgow - Adam Smith Business School

detail.title: Fiscal News and the Macroeconomy: Evidence from UK Budget Announcements
detail.abstract: This paper studies how fiscal news affects the macroeconomy. We use a novel identification strategy to isolate fiscal policy news shocks using high-frequency responses of financial markets to periodic and comprehensive fiscal announcements covering spending, taxation and debt issuance in the United Kingdom. Inside a local projections framework, we track the transmission of fiscal news shocks to yields on government debt, and then to output, prices, broader financial markets, households and firms. A negative fiscal news shock leads to sell-offs in both Gilts and Sterling, leading to tighter financial conditions, imported inflation, and depressed economic activity. The negative news leads to higher deficits through reduced tax collection without offsetting spending reductions. The Bank of England is on average slow to offset tighter financial conditions, however monetary offset appears to be stronger in the era of central bank independence and inflation targeting. We find meaningful heterogeneity in macro responses depending on the state of the business cycle and sign of the shock.

title: Public and expert preferences for biodiversity metrics and the implications for shadow pricing
affiliations: , University of Exeter, University of Trento and University of Exeter

detail.title: Public and expert preferences for biodiversity metrics and the implications for shadow pricing
detail.abstract: Biodiversity metrics are critical across a myriad of policy arenas, from Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) disclosures to international agreements and biodiversity offsetting schemes. However, the welfare implications of biodiversity metric selection remain poorly understood. We use a choice experiment to elicit preferences over key terrestrial biodiversity attributes from the British public, ecologists, and practitioners in the financial sector, avoiding problematic money-biodiversity trade-offs. Instead, elicited preferences are used to construct a welfare-based biodiversity metric that could underpin shadow pricing in pursuit of biodiversity policy targets, analogous to cost-based approaches in climate policies. All three groups prioritise enhancing species richness, preserving genetic distinctiveness, and preventing extinctions. In contrast, they show practical indifference to intactness measures, despite their widespread use in biodiversity policy, crediting, and ESG reporting. A case study of restoration site selection across Great Britain highlights the potential for substantial welfare and cost differences depending on which biodiversity metric guides policy decisions, and the large gains that a utility-based metric offers.

title: The Impact of Ozone Pollution on Hospitalizations
affiliations: Peking University, Peking University, Institute for Economic and Social Research, Jinan University and Peking University - National School of Development

detail.title: The Impact of Ozone Pollution on Hospitalizations

declarations.declarationOfInterest: MISSING
declarations.funderStatement: MISSING

detail.abstract: This paper estimates the impacts of ozone pollution on hospitalizations, medical expenditure, and in-hospital mortality using inpatient admission records from 1,087 hospitals in China between 2017 and 2021. Leveraging an instrumental variable based on ozone concentrations in nearby upwind cities, we find that ozone significantly increases all-cause hospitalizations and medical expenditure. Ozone elevates hospital admissions across a broader range of diseases than previously documented, and the hospitalization cost of 1-standard deviation increase in ozone is larger than that of PM2.5. Ozone reduces the average number of doctors per inpatient and increases the all-cause in-hospital mortality rate in emergency departments, suggesting that ozone-induced surges in healthcare demand generate hospital crowding, which lowers the quality of care and worsens patient outcomes.

title: Documentation Gap Analysis: Independent Audit of TGA COVID-19 Vaccine Safety Monitoring Plan

detail.title: Documentation Gap Analysis: Independent Audit of TGA COVID-19 Vaccine Safety Monitoring Plan

declarations.declarationOfInterest: I do not have any personal or financial relationship with other parties related to this research.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable.
declarations.funderStatement: This is self funded research.

detail.abstract:
This independent audit systematically evaluates the TGA COVID-19 Vaccine Safety Monitoring Plan (February 2021), which operationalised National Cabinet's commitment to enhanced pharmacovigilance under provisional approval across 68.4 million doses (91.2% of Australia's rollout) — addressing regulatory governance's core accountability problem: enhanced monitoring claims cannot be independently verified when underlying processes remain undocumented.

Findings reveal systematic documentation failures without precedent in Australian provisional medicine regulation. Only 3 of 20 Plan-specified outputs (15%) are fully documented; 17 (85%) are partially or not documented — despite TGA organising 2,218+ pages by Plan objectives for the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC) in September 2024. TGA reports 148 signals investigated and 57 regulatory actions taken, yet no audit trail links signals to actions or accounts for 91 unresolved signals. The OAIC confirmed the absence of implementation records.

Senior TGA officials testified before the Senate (9 October 2025) that monitoring occurred through "day-to-day processes" without systematic Plan tracking. TGA cannot demonstrate documented compliance with its own Safety Monitoring Plan — a regulatory accountability failure of serious consequence for the largest provisional medicine rollout in Australia's history.

The open-source methodology applies ISO 19011:2018, ANAO guidance, and OSINT principles to public records and FOI responses, published under CC BY 4.0 — fully open access and independently replicable.

title: Modeling Disease Comorbidity Among Medicare Beneficiaries Through Social Determinants of Health: Advances in Multi-Target Machine Learning
affiliations: University of Rhode Island, Independent, University of Rhode Island and University of Rhode Island

detail.title: Modeling Disease Comorbidity Among Medicare Beneficiaries Through Social Determinants of Health: Advances in Multi-Target Machine Learning

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None.
declarations.funderStatement: None.

detail.abstract: Amid proposed 2025 U.S. federal budget cuts targeting physician payments, vaccines, and capital equipment, ensuring accurate and equitable diagnoses for Medicare beneficiaries has become increasingly critical. This study addresses that need by developing a model that integrates altruistic values and social determinants of health (SDOH) to predict five common comorbidities among beneficiaries-high blood pressure, stroke, depression, emphysema, and diabetes-across three COVID-era Medicare cohorts (Spring 2020, Fall 2020, Winter 2021). Utilizing survey data from the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, we implement an optimized multi-target Radial Basis Function Neural Network (K4-MRBFN) and apply Shapley values from explainable AI (XAI) to assess feature importance and model transparency. K4-MRBFN consistently performed well with at least 89% accuracy across all cohorts. Income and rent payment ability emerged as the strongest predictors, highlighting financial stress as a key risk factor during the pandemic. Age, sex, and social connectedness were also influential, while access to food, home supplies, and medication had less impact. Depression was closely linked to unmet basic needs (excluding medication), underscoring persistent social support gaps. The current study findings highlight the importance of incorporating SDOH and ethical frameworks in evaluating disease states using novel advances in AI-driven healthcare tools.

title: Critically Evaluate the Legislative and Regulatory Steps Taken in Response to White Collar Crimes After the Financial Crisis in the UK and US

detail.title: Critically Evaluate the Legislative and Regulatory Steps Taken in Response to White Collar Crimes After the Financial Crisis in the UK and US
detail.abstract: The impacts of the financial crisis which was at its peak between 2007-2008 are still visible in the financial markets across the globe. It has brought about the most prevalent change in the world’s economic and financial landscape. The economies of United Kingdom and United States has been deemed to have suffered from the hardest hit of the global financial crisis. It has essentially originated from credit markets in economically dominant countries such as UK and US, and the wrath of the crisis has then travelled across Europe. The causes behind the crisis has appeared to be manifold. This thesis considers one of the causes behind the financial crisis, closely albeit the author acknowledges that it is not the sole cause of the financial crisis but it is one of the significant causes behind the crisis. The focus of the thesis is thus white collar crimes associated with the financial crisis in both UK and US markets. The research follows on to critically assess the regulatory and legislative approaches taken towards white collar crimes in both the jurisdiction. Although, in both countries many strong provisions have been made followed by the financial crisis to tackle white collar crimes but amongst other failures, they have failed to ensure prosecution against the high profile perpetrators who committed the white collar crimes associated with the financial crisis. The research criticises the shortcomings of the responses taken in both countries to the extent to which they were ineffective whilst acknowledging the successful responses which brought about effective results like recovery of funds in the form of fines.

detail.abstract: Vaccination hesitancy has become a worldwide public health issue that is jeopardizing routine immunization programs and causing vaccine-preventable diseases to reappear. For several socioeconomic and cultural settings, this has become a public health challenge. These documents combine evidence concerning the prevalence, the factors influencing, and the impact, on hesitancy related to vaccines among parent and guardians of children. This analysis merges peer-reviewed narratives, policy documents, and surveys between 2015 and 2025 and integrates qualitative and quantitative analysis to map out certain aspects and contextual elements. There exists evidence that indicates a significant positive correlation between hesitancy regarding pediatric vaccines and a reduction in overall vaccination rates, with a particular emphasis on the rate of vaccination for measles and other multi-dose childhood vaccines. (Elawad et al.). Element of hesitancy involves absence of accurate and contextualized risk analysis, lack of health knowledge, socioeconomic disadvantage, culturally and religiously grounded beliefs, and inequitable distribution of healthcare services and professional trust.

title: Modelling Diabetes Risk Factors in Women: Insights From Logistic Regression and PCA on the Pima Indian Dataset

detail.title: Modelling Diabetes Risk Factors in Women: Insights From Logistic Regression and PCA on the Pima Indian Dataset

declarations.funderStatement: No funding.

detail.abstract: This study investigates diabetes risk factors among women using the Pima Indian Diabetes dataset, publicly available from the National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (NIDDK). Principal Component Analysis (PCA) was applied to identify the key clinical and physiological features, including blood sugar level, Body Mass Index (BMI), number of pregnancies, and diabetes pedigree function, that are responsible for increasing the risk of diabetes. Logistic regression was then used to model and predict diabetes risk based on these features. The model was well fitted with an accuracy of 78.26%, with moderate sensitivity (58.21%) and high specificity (89%). Applying PCA for feature selection improved model performance, and increased the prediction accuracy to 82.47%. These findings highlight the importance of dimensional reduction and feature selection in improving the model interpretability and predictive performance. The study recommends the use of PCA in combination with logistic regression to improve the accuracy in identifying significant factors and predict diabetes risk in women.

title: Reducing Waste through Anti-Fraud Enforcement: Evidence from Hospital Admission Cases
affiliations: Emory University - Department of Health Policy and Management and Boston University

detail.title: Reducing Waste through Anti-Fraud Enforcement: Evidence from Hospital Admission Cases
detail.abstract: The use of federal anti-fraud laws to address unnecessary medical care is controversial. Targeted providers frequently argue that, in their judgment, the treatment in question was appropriate. We examine the effects of anti-fraud litigation against hospitals for over-admitting patients from the emergency department, using 100% Medicare claims for 2005-2019 and a design based on the staggered rollout of these lawsuits. We find that anti-fraud lawsuits reduced admission rates by 3.6 percentage points without increasing mortality rates. We estimate five-year savings to Medicare of $1.3 billion. Our results suggest that anti-fraud enforcement can be successful in reducing costly, unnecessary care.

title: Racial Preferences at a Texas Medical School

detail.title: Racial Preferences at a Texas Medical School
detail.abstract: Whether and how race is used in selective admissions remains a central question in higher education and civil rights law. In Students for Fair Admissions v. Harvard (2023), the Supreme Court held that race-based aﬃrmative action in college admissions violates the Equal Protection Clause, purportedly ending the practice. This report examines admissions at a public medical school in the pre-SFFA period. Using applicant-level data on over 11,000 applications to Texas Tech University Health Sciences Center Medical School for the 2021 and 2022 cycles, I relate admission decisions to academic merit (MCAT, GPA, science GPA), race, gender, and situational judgment (Casper) scores. Summary statistics, academic-index decompositions, and logistic regression models provide strong evidence of racial preferences: African American and Hispanic applicants are preferred relative to academically similar White and Asian applicants. Counterfactual and preference-removal analyses quantify the magnitude of these disparities. The findings document the kind of race-based preferences that SFF A was meant to address and establish a baseline for assessing whether admissions practice changed after the decision.

title: OnlyFans, More Than Taxpayers: Toward a Compliance Aesthetic in the Gig Economy
affiliations: Pace University - School of Law

detail.title: OnlyFans, More Than Taxpayers: Toward a Compliance Aesthetic in the Gig Economy
detail.abstract:
This Article examines how creators on the subscription-based platform OnlyFans understand and navigate their federal tax obligations, with particular attention to peer-to-peer advice shared in publicly accessible online forums. As independent contractors, OnlyFans creators must track income, manage expenses, and comply with complex self-employment tax rules. Yet little scholarly attention has been paid to how these creators talk about taxation or how tax compliance figures into their understanding of their work. This Article argues that tax discourse among OnlyFans creators reflects a distinctive rhetorical and cultural orientation that frames compliance not as a burdensome imposition, but as a meaningful component of professional identity. I call this phenomenon the compliance aesthetic: a self-conscious performance of legitimacy in which adherence to tax and legal norms operates as a claim to moral credibility and economic seriousness in a stigmatized line of work.

Drawing on qualitative analysis of posts from Reddit and the TurboTax Community, the Article shows that creators overwhelmingly seek to comply with tax law. Their discourse is procedural and entrepreneurial rather than resistant, centering on forms, deductions, recordkeeping, and long-term planning. Legitimacy is rarely asserted directly; instead, it is enacted through routine compliance talk that treats taxation as an ordinary feature of running a business. Although stigma and disclosure concerns arise—particularly in relation to family members, financial institutions, and software interfaces—creators navigate these risks strategically rather than retreating from compliance. Across both platforms, creators themselves, not tax professionals, perform the primary interpretive labor, sharing heuristics and normalizing compliance as part of adult economic participation.

The Article proceeds in five parts. Part I provides background on OnlyFans and its economic model. Part II situates the study within literature on gig workers, whose tax discourse often emphasizes confusion or resistance. Part III describes the research design and methodology. Part IV presents the findings through the lens of labor identity and legitimacy. Part V offers normative recommendations for the Internal Revenue Service and tax professionals, arguing that platform-aware guidance should recognize creators as proactive legal actors. In doing so, the Article repositions tax reporting as a site of identity formation, economic self-assertion, and cultural meaning-making among nontraditional workers.

title: Transparency Features in Robo-Advice: Evidence, Mechanisms, and EU Policy Implications for Trust, Reliance, and Financial Inclusion
